lines: Look at row 9.
Only one square is empty, at row 9, column 1.
Eight numbers are already there. The only one missing is 5.
Look for the number 3 in the top-left box.
3 is already placed at row 1 column 4 and row 7 column 3, and that rules out the other empty squares in the top-left box.
The only square left for 3 is row 2, column 2.
Check which numbers can go at row 5, column 5.
Its row already has 2, 7 and 8.
Its column adds 1, 3, 5 and 6.
Its 3 by 3 box adds 9.
The only number left is 4.
In the top-middle box, the number 8 can only go in row 2 column 4 and row 2 column 6.
All of those squares are in row 2.
Whichever one it is, 8 in row 2 must sit inside this box.
So you can remove 8 from row 2, column 9.
In column 9, the number 7 can only go in row 5 column 9 and row 6 column 9.
All of those squares are inside the middle-right box.
So the 7 of that box must be one of these squares too.
So you can remove 7 from row 5, column 8.
In column 3, look at row 4 column 3 and row 5 column 3.
Those two squares can only hold 2 and 9.
So 2 and 9 are used up there, and no other square in column 3 can have them.
So you can remove 9 from row 7, column 3.
In the bottom-middle box, the numbers 1 and 5 can only go in row 7 column 5 and row 8 column 5.
Those two squares must hold those two numbers.
So nothing else can go in them.
So you can remove 3 from row 8, column 5.
In column 4, look at row 2 column 4, row 5 column 4 and row 6 column 4.
Those three squares can only hold 2, 6 and 8.
So 2, 6 and 8 are used up there, and no other square in column 4 can have them.
So you can remove 6 from row 9, column 4.
In column 7, the numbers 6, 8 and 9 can only go in row 1 column 7, row 2 column 7 and row 5 column 7.
Those three squares must hold those three numbers.
So nothing else can go in them.
So you can remove 5 from row 5, column 7.
Follow the number 7 in column 1 and column 9.
In these lines, 7 can only go in row 5 and row 6.
Each line needs one 7, so these two lines will use up the 7 of those crossing lines.
So you can remove 7 from row 5, column 8.
The middle square at row 7, column 7 can only be 1 or 6.
It connects to row 1, column 7, which is 6 or 7, and to row 8, column 7, which is 1 or 7.
Whichever number the middle square takes, one of those two squares must become 7.
Any square that sees both of them cannot be 7.
So you can remove 7 from row 6, column 7.
Follow the number 1 in column 4, column 5 and column 6.
In these lines, 1 can only go in row 1, row 5 and row 9.
Each line needs one 1, so these three lines will use up the 1 of those crossing lines.
So you can remove 1 from row 1, column 8.
